timeline.title: Senior Software Engineer
bullets: Designed and built a modular knowledge-management and RAG template with Tesseract OCR for scanned documents, configurable ingestion modules, and Kerberos/JWT authentication. Adopted as the account standard and used by another team for contract-field extraction.

Built adaptive, schema-driven extraction with LangGraph, LangChain, and ChromaDB: retrieve and rerank source chunks, return fields with context and page references, and retry only unresolved fields. Supports extensible presets and on-demand schemas. Recognised in the CIO newsletter in 2026 for the template.

Leading the technical review and phased modernisation of a Python and React infrastructure dashboard: restructuring the backend, removing spreadsheet dependencies, and introducing REST APIs. Both applications are now deployed on Rancher; a Prefect-to-SQL data pipeline is planned.

Brought an existing PDF clause-extraction application into production: improved Python configuration and paths, adapted Tesseract OCR for Linux, introduced GitLab CI, and packaged the embedding model from Nexus into the container. The Python RAG API and React application were deployed on Rancher and have run reliably for about a year.

Built a .NET API to make existing business data accessible to other teams, using Entity Framework Core with SQL Server. Prepared Helm and Flux configuration with the onboarding skill and deployed the service to Rancher.
Improved the memory footprint of financial-data APIs through LINQ query optimisation and related code changes.

Guide teammates delivering modernisation work across teams, reviewing implementation approaches and technical decisions. Drive adoption of the toolchain team’s GitLab CI templates and the use of pipeline-built container images in Rancher deployments.

Replaced manual deployment-template setup with a guided Rancher onboarding skill. It collects service requirements, prepares and publishes repositories, validates configuration, and supports later service additions using the firm’s existing deployment conventions.
Extended the enterprise knowledge system to Claude Code and Copilot CLI through MCP. Access is checked by the knowledge service before it issues time-limited credentials to authorised users.

Developed an Informatica migration plugin that combines workflow discovery, application-wide assessment and equivalent Python/Prefect code generation. It identifies complexity and common patterns, provides executive summaries, and retains progress across skills while following the firm’s runtime and project conventions.

Built an API to make financial data available to applications and provided a working reference for the team. Established clear responsibilities and project conventions, then walked the team through the design and how to extend it.
Resolved browser-deployment issues blocking a team’s regulatory scraping workflow, providing a working browser runtime on Rancher and configuring the connection needed by the application.

Modernised legacy .NET applications into microservices across multiple programmes — decomposed monoliths, upgraded frameworks, and containerised services for cloud-native deployment on Kubernetes via Rancher.

Migrated seven Solace messaging services to Kubernetes with zero post-deployment defects, independently leading three migrations. Resolved connection failover, message redelivery and consumer-group binding issues.

Contributed to critical incident recovery during a US data centre outage at quarter-end — mobilised as part of the global SME team (India, US, EMEA) to help restore trading operations under time pressure.
Recognised in the CIO newsletter for contributions to the clause-extraction application’s production delivery.
Mentors junior developers through architecture reviews and code quality standards; conducts technical interviews aligned with the client's engineering and cultural standards.
Uses xUnit and pytest for unit testing and SonarQube static analysis in the CI pipeline.
Uses agentic AI tools for architecture exploration, debugging and implementation, alongside code review and testing.

Prototyped a shared hub for internal engineering resources, bringing skills, MCP integrations and modernisation reporting into one place while keeping them as separate modules. Built the initial reporting module, which other developers have since extended.

recentWork.title: A modular foundation for knowledge and document extraction.
recentWork.summary: The template combines OCR for scanned documents, adaptive field extraction, and built-in authentication. Teams can tailor its modules and extraction schemas to their use case, while developers can access enterprise knowledge through controlled MCP integrations.
recentWork.detail: Adaptive extraction uses LangGraph and LangChain to build schema-driven retrieval queries for each requested field. It retrieves relevant chunks from ChromaDB, reranks them by similarity, and constructs an LLM prompt with source material. Results include the field value, supporting context, page number, and model-reported confidence. Subsequent retrieval passes target only unresolved fields, keeping repeated context and unnecessary model input down.
recentWork.outcome: A reusable, configurable foundation for enterprise knowledge and document extraction, adopted for a contract-field extraction application.
recentWork.intro: A shared foundation for enterprise knowledge use cases, extended to coding agents with controlled access.
recentWork.context: Designed a reusable knowledge-management template for document extraction, internal knowledge search, and termsheet comparison. Adopted as the account standard, it has also been used by another team to implement contract-field extraction.
recentWork.notes: Built-in authentication supports Kerberos and JWT-based API keys. The MCP integration supports Claude Code and Copilot CLI; the knowledge service checks required Swarm-group membership before issuing a JWT-based key with a 30-day expiry.
recentWork.recognition: Recognised in the CIO newsletter in 2026 for the knowledge-management template, which another team adopted for contract-field extraction.

capabilities.title: Extraction that follows the missing fields
capabilities.body: Retrieves and reranks source chunks for the requested schema, then returns field values with context, page references, and confidence. Further passes focus on fields still missing.

capabilities.title: Reusable presets or on-demand schemas
capabilities.body: Teams can extend predefined extraction presets or define field names, data types, validation rules, and examples on the fly to try a new document use case.

capabilities.title: Modules teams can tailor
capabilities.body: Vertical slice architecture lets teams disable modules such as Jira ingestion through environment variables, or remove them entirely. Tesseract OCR supports scanned documents, with authentication built into the template.

recentWork.title: Taking applications from implementation to production.
recentWork.context: A dashboard gave stakeholders useful visibility into application infrastructure, but its tightly coupled Python script, spreadsheet dependencies, and file-based data exchange made it difficult to maintain and prepare for production.
recentWork.summary: Currently leading the technical review and phased modernisation of a Python and React dashboard that gives stakeholders a view of application infrastructure from ServiceNow. The work is replacing a large, tightly coupled script and spreadsheet-based configuration with a structured backend and REST APIs. The React application and Python API are now deployed on Rancher; further data-pipeline work is ongoing.
recentWork.detail: After reviewing the codebase with its developer, I broke the work into phases: separate frontend and backend responsibilities, restructure the Python code, remove spreadsheet dependencies, and replace direct consumption of generated JSON files with REST endpoints. The planned next stage uses Prefect flows to collect data into SQL, with the Python API serving it to React.
recentWork.intro: Building the service, improving the codebase, and carrying the work through deployment.
recentWork.outcome: The dashboard has a better-structured codebase, with its React application and Python API deployed on Rancher. The Prefect and SQL data pipeline remains planned.

recentWork.title: Taking PDF clause extraction into production.
recentWork.context: An existing PDF clause-extraction application had a Python RAG backend and React interface, but needed substantial code and deployment improvements before it could run reliably in production.
recentWork.summary: I reworked configuration and hardcoded paths, adapted the Tesseract OCR integration for Linux, and brought the application onto GitLab and its CI pipeline. I also changed how the embedding model was packaged for deployment. After resolving application and environment issues, the service was successfully deployed on Rancher and has been running reliably in production for about a year.
recentWork.detail: The Python API used RAG, Tesseract OCR, FAISS, and an all-MiniLM embedding model. The model was initially kept directly in the source repository. I changed the container build to retrieve its ZIP artifact from Nexus and include it through the Docker runtime template. Alongside the OCR changes, configuration cleanup, and GitLab CI adoption, I worked through issues across the application and deployment until the production release succeeded.
recentWork.intro: Improving an existing clause-extraction application and carrying it through a successful production release.
recentWork.outcome: Successfully deployed on Rancher and running reliably in production for about a year.
recentWork.recognition: Recognised in the CIO newsletter for contributions to the clause-extraction application’s production delivery.

recentWork.title: Encoding deployment conventions into onboarding.
recentWork.summary: Teams were cloning deployment templates and editing placeholders by hand to onboard services. I turned that setup into a guided skill that collects requirements, prepares the repositories, checks the configuration, and publishes the changes. It also supports adding services to an existing setup.
recentWork.detail: The skill follows the firm’s deployment model: application Helm charts for deployments, services and image versions; infrastructure charts for ingress and ConfigMaps; and a Flux tenant connecting the charts to Rancher. It creates the required repositories and branches, supports Avi ingress, and validates the generated setup using Helm and kubectl.
recentWork.outcome: Service onboarding and subsequent additions follow the same configuration, repository and validation workflow.
recentWork.intro: Replacing repeated template editing with a guided workflow that follows the firm’s deployment conventions.

recentWork.title: From Informatica workflows to Python and Prefect.
recentWork.summary: Developed a migration plugin that takes teams from understanding existing Informatica workflows to generating equivalent Python/Prefect implementations. It can work across an application, identifying migration difficulty and common patterns, producing an executive summary, and retaining progress between runs.
recentWork.detail: The plugin separates discovery, assessment and code generation into focused skills. Discovery accepts manual evidence or Informatica XML exports and records missing behaviour and unresolved references. Assessment examines complexity and commonality across workflows. Generated code follows the firm’s Python project structure and AutoSys, Rancher and Prefect conventions. Each skill’s progress is tracked in JSON so the process can continue across runs.
recentWork.notes: The discovery step keeps extracted metadata, assumptions and missing runtime details explicit. Parameter files, scheduler details, production run history and SME notes provide additional context when available for downstream assessment and code generation.
recentWork.outcome: A connected migration process with workflow findings, executive reporting, generated implementations, and retained progress.
recentWork.intro: Taking legacy workflows through discovery and migration planning to equivalent Python/Prefect code.

recentWork.title: An API for financial data.
recentWork.summary: Built an API to make financial data available to applications and provided a working reference the team could extend. I organised the service around clear responsibilities and walked the team through the design, so ongoing development had a consistent starting point.
recentWork.detail: The implementation separates request handling, business logic and data access into controller, service and repository layers. Consistent naming and project structure make it clear where new behaviour belongs. The handover covered both the code and how to extend the service.
recentWork.outcome: A financial data API and a shared reference for continued development.
recentWork.intro: Making financial data available through an API, with a working implementation and clear conventions for the team.

recentWork.title: Unblocking browser automation on Rancher.
recentWork.summary: Resolved browser-deployment issues that were blocking a regulatory-web scraping use case. Configured a working browser runtime on Rancher and the connection the team’s application needed to use it.
recentWork.detail: The Crawl4AI application needed Chromium running in the firm’s Kubernetes environment. The team’s initial approach had encountered deployment and vulnerability concerns. I used the official Playwright image, created a Flux-managed Helm release, and adjusted the startup arguments and CDP connection settings to get the runtime working.
recentWork.outcome: The team had a working browser runtime for its scraping application.
recentWork.intro: Removing a browser-runtime blocker from a team’s regulatory scraping workflow.

recentWork.title: A prototype hub for organising our tools.
recentWork.summary: Prototyped a shared home for custom skills, MCP integrations, and modernisation reporting. The aim is to make these resources easier to find while keeping each tool as a separate application.
recentWork.detail: Built the hub with Vite module federation, loading separate microfrontends into a configurable shell. Kubernetes ConfigMaps define the module entries. The skills module retrieves content from GitLab, and the MCP module lists available integrations. I also built the initial reporting module using ServiceNow APIs and other sources; other developers have since extended it.
recentWork.outcome: An organisational prototype for finding and accessing internal engineering tools.
recentWork.intro: A prototype to bring scattered engineering resources into one place.

recentWork.title: Making business data accessible through an API.
recentWork.summary: Built a .NET API over existing business data that other teams previously had no API to access. Carried the service from implementation through deployment on Rancher.
recentWork.detail: Built a .NET and Entity Framework Core API over existing SQL Server tables and views, making business data accessible to other teams. I prepared its Helm and Flux configuration using the onboarding skill and deployed it to Rancher.

recentWork.title: Reducing memory usage in financial-data APIs.
recentWork.summary: Reduced the memory footprint of existing financial-data APIs through LINQ query optimisation and related implementation changes.
recentWork.detail: The changes covered LINQ queries and related service code in existing financial applications, reducing the APIs’ memory footprint.
